newsitem.title: INDIA: India urges EU to reconsider seafood import ban.
newsitem.headline: India urges EU to reconsider seafood import ban.

text.p: India appealed to the European Union on Tuesday to reconsider a ban on Indian seafood imports which the bloc imposed because of health worries.

The Commerce Ministry said the government would ensure its fish processing plants meet the standards of the EU, which on Monday announced it was cutting off fishery products from India, Bangladesh and Madagascar.
"We are committed to stringent hygiene standards, and we will conform to their levels," a Ministry spokeswoman told Reuters.
The EU's move followed recent visits by European Commission inspectors.
"The inspections showed serious deficiencies in...the hygiene quality of raw material and in processing operations," the Commission said in a statement.
"It is entirely on health and safety reasons," Heino Marius, economic and commercial secretary at the European Commission's delegation in New Delhi, told Reuters.
The Commission's decision to halt imports of products such as shrimp and squid was temporary and will be reviewed before November 30, the EU's executive said in Brussels on Monday.
The ban has already taken effect, although fish products which are being shipped to the 15-nation EU may be admitted before August 15, subject to satisfactory sample testing.
"Some traces of bacteria were found during inspections of goods when they reached Europe," Marius said. "Our prime concern is the health of the European children."
The Commission said the inspections showed the level of control by the national authorities was inadequate.
But the Commerce Ministry spokeswoman said Indian plants had "by and large" met the EU's standards, and a total ban on Indian products was too sweeping.
"We have been conforming to the stringent standards by and large, and if there have been some stray incidents, then there should be some discretion before imposing a total ban," she said.
"We are saying don't go for a total ban and in the meanwhile we are upgrading the units that are lagging."
Indian and European officials said the two sides would meet to discuss the ban. ($1=35.7 rupees)
